verdict.rationale: Supermemory's container tags are documented as a hard namespace boundary. Memories in one tag are never returned by a search scoped to another, and both `add` and `search` take a `containerTag`. The docs explicitly recommend scoping each end-user or tenant to its own tag. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-agent or per-application scoping (only user/tenant examples are shown), evidence that isolation is enforced server-side beyond the client-supplied tag, and independent or hands-on corroboration that no leakage occurs.

support.subject: As a developer, I can scope memories per user, agent, or application so one tenant's memories never leak into another's retrieval

citations.quote: A container tag is a hard boundary — its own namespace. Memories in one tag are never returned by a search scoped to another tag.
every memory tagged with `user_alex` lives in its own isolated space, completely separate from memories tagged `user_jordan`
Scope each end-user (or tenant) to a container tag.
const results = await client.search({ q: "where does Alex work?", containerTag: "user_123", include: { relatedMemories: true }, });
A space keeps a team's documents, memories, and profile context focused, so AI retrieves the right knowledge without mixing unrelated work.
